title: Air Quality State Implementation Plans: New Hampshire Vehicle Inspection Repeal

ai_data.summary_of_main_idea: The EPA proposes to approve a State Implementation Plan (SIP) revision from New Hampshire to repeal its mandatory Motor Vehicle Inspection and Maintenance (I/M) program for air quality control.
ai_data.challenges: The proposal fails to provide required modeling demonstrating that repealing the I/M program will not interfere with attainment or reasonable progress under Clean Air Act Section 110(l). Furthermore, public docket rendering errors under APA 5 U.S.C. § 553 deprived citizens of full technical documentation.

references.title: Yale Law Journal: Notice-and-Comment Rulemaking in the Digital Age
CRS Report: Administrative Procedure Act Rulemaking Guidelines

ai_data.proposed_comment:
To: Environmental Protection Agency (EPA)
Re: Docket No. EPA-R01-OAR-2026-2147-0001

(1) Introduction & Primary Argument:
We submit this comment regarding the proposed repeal of New Hampshire's Motor Vehicle Inspection and Maintenance (I/M) program. Under Clean Air Act § 110(l), 42 U.S.C. § 7410(l), the EPA cannot approve a SIP revision if it interferes with attainment or maintenance of National Ambient Air Quality Standards (NAAQS). The current record lacks sufficient empirical non-interference demonstration.

(2) Legal Rationale & Alternative Language:
We request that EPA defer final approval until comprehensive mobile source emissions modeling (MOVES3) is published demonstrating no net increase in NOx or VOC emissions.
